label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article I, Section 2, Clause 5. The House chooses its Speaker and other officers and alone has the power to impeach. It reads: “The House of Representatives shall chuse their Speaker and other Officers; and shall have the sole Power of Impeachment.”
This story is about a congressional choice on an impeachment resolution.
In 1787, article I, Section 2, Clause 5 of the Constitution, signed September 17, 1787, says the House of Representatives "shall have the sole Power of Impeachment."
House members voted to send the resolution to a committee.
That step set the matter aside for the rest of this Congress.
The strongest argument against this is that a floor vote referred the resolution to committee rather than putting impeachment itself to a full vote this power calls for.
We read this clause to mean the House alone holds this power and may refer impeachable matters to committee.
This keeps the choice with the elected House.
